findings.statement: Rocq kernel-checks that any finite real-coefficient weighted sum of basis functions whose left limits at xi=1 are zero also has left limit zero. Exact equality on a nonempty terminal interval with either the constant invariant 1 or p_star*xi/(1-xi), for p_star>0, yields a contradiction. This proves NC-SAME-SPACE under its frozen finite-span assumptions and does not imply that a distinct Petrov test space or analytic invariant component works.
assumptions_used: The span contains finitely many basis functions.
All expansion coefficients are finite real constants independent of xi.
Every basis function has left limit zero at xi=1.
Claimed representation is pointwise equality on a nonempty terminal interval.
p_star>0 for compactified momentum.
counterevidence_refs: CAS_CONTRACT C-PETROV deliberately changes the test space, and C-ANALYTIC adds a separate invariant component; neither is covered by the same-space theorem.
unresolved: The proof uses the standard Rocq real-number library, whose Print Assumptions reports only its existing ClassicalDedekindReals and functional-extensionality dependencies; the proof adds no Axiom, Parameter, Admitted, or admit.

findings.statement: The strongest admission case is that a distinct conservative test space containing exact 1 and p evades NC-SAME-SPACE while a terminal-vanishing trial space controls the endpoint. The decisive rejection case is that the sealed evidence supplies no fully specified pairing/local mass map, uniform inf-sup lower bound, nonsymmetric fermionic entropy proof, process-total shell/tail closure, binary64 bound, or net-deflation plan. Rocq kernel-checks the typed dependency implication petrov_dependency_gap, but that theorem audits the frozen evidence-status table and is not a mathematical impossibility theorem for all Petrov methods.
assumptions_used: All eleven G-EXT-FEASIBILITY obligations are binding.
A conditional mechanism is not Established evidence.
A missing theorem is INCONCLUSIVE, never an implicit pass.
No post-hoc conservation projection is allowed.
counterevidence_refs: A prospectively frozen trial/test pairing with a uniform inf-sup certificate and derived entropy inequality could reverse this verdict without contradicting NC-SAME-SPACE.
unresolved: Decisive falsifier: exhibit an interior state where the inf-sup bound vanishes, the p test diverges, entropy needs unavailable symmetry/positivity, or conservation occurs outside the weak form.
Verdict-changing evidence: one exact artifact discharging all candidate-specific and eleven common obligations, with no deferred implementation choice.

findings.statement: The strongest admission case is that one analytic equilibrium/invariant component plus vanishing local perturbations could own the full half-line and remove the finite-Y_max tail split. The opposing case remains decisive on present bytes: no unique differentiable coefficient map, exact pre-quadrature conservation/entropy theorem, single-consumer tail authority, bypass exclusion, prospective conditioning/binary64 certificate, or exact non-isomorphism to B3-v2 is supplied. Rocq kernel-checks analytic_dependency_gap at the novelty obligation, but the missing scientific premises are encoded audit facts rather than proved no-go theorems.
assumptions_used: The analytic component must be part of one total representation, not a second tail oracle or correction surface.
Every binding property must be fixed before output.
Basis/domain relabeling is not structural novelty.
Missing proof is INCONCLUSIVE.
counterevidence_refs: A single typed coefficient map with exact invariant ownership, a consumer-total half-line representation, and a formal operation-graph non-isomorphism proof could change the verdict.
unresolved: Decisive falsifier: singular/discontinuous coefficient map, a bypassable analytic component, a second tail consumer, or an exact reduction to B3-v2.
The compactified equilibrium baseline described externally is only SPECULATIVE and is not a closed analytic-component construction.

findings.statement: A finite reversible edge network with nonnegative symmetric conductances conditionally offers exact invariants, Pauli-compatible positivity, detailed balance, and a fermionic H-theorem. The simplest fixed dimensionless lattice fails the exact two-temperature finite-mass closure test, but that does not prove a universal moving-lattice no-go. The moving/remap candidate remains non-admitted because no theorem preserves occupations, invariants, reversibility, positivity, entropy, differentiability, tail enclosure, deterministic angular extension, and the cost bound across the continuous temperature domain. Rocq kernel-checks medvm_dependency_gap at the finite-m_e-shell obligation.
assumptions_used: Forward and reverse edges must be exactly on shell and share nonnegative conductance.
Temperature varies continuously over the frozen domain.
A fixed-lattice failure does not imply every moving-remap scheme is impossible.
Stochastic angular sampling cannot satisfy the deterministic obligation.
Missing remap theorem is INCONCLUSIVE.
counterevidence_refs: A rigorous moving-lattice/remap theorem plus sparse deterministic edge factorization could overturn the current likely-no-go assessment.
unresolved: Decisive falsifier: any remap loses exact reversibility, invariants, Pauli bounds, entropy, differentiability, or exceeds the frozen edge/cost budget.
The fixed-lattice subroute is rejected; the broader moving-remap feasibility claim remains unproved rather than universally falsified.

findings.statement: No candidate supplies the binding exact operation-graph non-isomorphism proof against sealed B3-v2. Petrov and analytic-component variants are materially different readings of the externally proposed compactified DG outline, but their complete operators do not exist. MEDVM would be structurally distinct if a full on-shell moving edge/remap graph existed, but that graph is absent. Consequently local endpoint and dependency theorems cannot establish novelty or G-EXT-FEASIBILITY.
assumptions_used: Novelty is assessed against B3-v2 basis, finite-domain/tail ledger, mass solve, event trace, and A0-A4 graph as a whole.
A change of basis, domain coordinates, language, or compiler wrapper alone is not novelty.
A compiler can reduce authority divergence but does not prove physics independence.
counterevidence_refs: An exact bidirectional operation-DAG comparison proving that one fully specified candidate cannot be mapped to B3-v2 would change this verdict.
unresolved: PDR: preserve STOP/PRESERVE. The strongest admission steelman does not overcome missing novelty, shell, stability, binary64, and cost closure.
Any future exact artifact must pass all eleven binding obligations; a single non-PASS remains terminal and cannot be rescued by the local Rocq theorem.
